articles.topic: CSO first-time-buyer income, age, Help to Buy and mortgage-capacity analysis
articles.distinct_thesis: The CSO's €82,600 median transaction income becomes more useful when translated into a €330,400 standard four-times mortgage ceiling and contrasted with joint, sole and Help to Buy buyer profiles.

claim_checks.claim: 2024 first-time-buyer transactions numbered 30,480; median income was €82,600 and median age 36.
claim_checks.basis: CSO 17 November 2026 Frontier Series key findings.

claim_checks.claim: The 2022–2024 median-income increase was 12.2%, and the standard four-times illustration is €330,400.
claim_checks.basis: (82,600 / 73,600 - 1) × 100 = 12.228%; 82,600 × 4 = 330,400. Different annual cohorts and standard-rule illustration are stated explicitly.

claim_checks.claim: Joint and sole buyer median incomes imply a €152,000 difference under a mechanical four-times illustration.
Help to Buy recipient median income was €97,200 and the reported share was 18%.
claim_checks.basis: Quoted from CSO; the article does not recompute the share from potentially different effective denominators or claim causality.

articles.topic: CSO 2025 Compensation of Employees and why national wage-bill growth is not an individual pay rise
articles.distinct_thesis: The €6.9bn increase is a whole-economy compensation measure containing labour input and employer costs, so workers should not mistake its 4.35% growth for average salary growth.

claim_checks.claim: Compensation of Employees was €165.1584bn in 2025 versus €158.2687bn in 2024.
Public Administration, Education & Health accounted for €45.8bn or 27.8%.
claim_checks.basis: CSO key findings; identified as broad-sector total compensation, not typical pay.

claim_checks.claim: The male 58.1% share is not a like-for-like gender pay-gap measure.
claim_checks.basis: The source measure is aggregate compensation and the article expressly distinguishes composition, hours and employment effects.

articles.topic: Consumer Credit Directive protections applying from 20 November to BNPL, sub-€200 credit and agreements up to €100,000
articles.distinct_thesis: The useful household change is not that BNPL first becomes regulated, but that the revised 20 November framework extends standard information, withdrawal and automated-decision rights across a broader credit scope.

claim_checks.claim: Rules apply from 20 November 2026 and cover credit below €200, agreements up to €100,000 and additional products including BNPL.
claim_checks.basis: Department of Finance announcement and EUR-Lex application-date summary.

claim_checks.claim: Covered non-mortgage agreements up to €100,000 have a 14-day withdrawal right.
claim_checks.basis: Department announcement; mortgages and applicable scope are expressly excluded/qualified in copy.

claim_checks.claim: Automated creditworthiness processing carries explanation, human-intervention and review rights.
claim_checks.basis: Department announcement; article states review does not guarantee approval.

claim_checks.claim: BNPL was already regulated in Ireland before 20 November.
claim_checks.basis: CCPC and Central Bank consumer guidance say authorisation requirements have applied since 2022.
